confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web search summaries. These were Numbeo, Wise and other national Bolivia averages from around October 2026 (for example, cappuccino about Bs 19.75, draft beer about Bs 14.50 and a mid-range meal for two about Bs 159), plus a 2026 Uyuni budget guide (basic restaurant meal about $4-6, tourist restaurants about $8-15 per person). Because Uyuni is a tourist hub, I set the anchors above the national averages. The boliviano peg ended at the end of June 2026 and the rate floated to roughly 10-12 Bs/USD by July-November, so my conversions assume a rate of about 11-11.7. Prices in bolivianos are also rising, which adds uncertainty. Draft beer is not common in Uyuni, so the beer anchor reflects bottled local beer (Paceña/Potosina) served in a restaurant. I found no aggregated cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices. The cocktail and wine figures come from the local price relationship to beer (roughly 1.8x and 1.5x) and one review reporting 210 Bs as the cheapest wine bottle at a restaurant. They are the least certain food and drink anchors. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for the July high (dry) season, based on general knowledge; I did not check any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Started from Numbeo national and city averages for Bolivia (La Paz, Sucre, Cochabamba). Raised them toward the tourist end, by analogy with other remote Andean tourist bases such as San Pedro de Atacama (but cheaper) and Puno or Copacabana. Uyuni's isolation and tour-driven demand push restaurant and hotel prices above those in Bolivian cities of similar size.
